subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: records the electrical activity of individual neurons in the cortex.
parts: penetrating shanks of silicon or flexible polymer, each thinner than a human hair

subsystems.name: Implantation system
subsystems.role: places hundreds of electrodes precisely without hitting blood vessels.

subsystems.name: Implanted electronics
subsystems.role: amplifies, digitises and wirelessly moves neural data through intact skin.
parts: hermetically sealed titanium or ceramic case

subsystems.name: Decoding software
subsystems.role: turns raw spike activity into a movement intention.

subsystems.name: Effector and control loop
subsystems.role: does something with the decoded intention.
parts: functional electrical stimulation of the user's own muscles

subsystems.name: Sensory feedback channel
subsystems.role: returns touch and limb-position information to the brain.

buildSteps.title: Choose the electrode design
buildSteps.detail: Rigid silicon shanks record cleanly but provoke scarring; flexible polymer threads move with the brain but are difficult to insert. The trade-off sets the achievable implant lifetime.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the array
buildSteps.detail: In a cleanroom, photolithography and thin-film metal deposition pattern conductive tracks onto a wafer or polymer sheet, which is then insulated and cut into individual shanks with bare recording tips.

buildSteps.title: Build and seal the electronics
buildSteps.detail: A custom chip amplifies and digitises hundreds of channels; a coil receives power and a radio sends data out through the skin. The package is hermetically sealed and soak-tested in saline.

buildSteps.title: Test in animals
buildSteps.detail: Arrays and electronics are implanted in non-human primates and pigs and left for months to measure signal quality, tissue reaction and implant survival.

buildSteps.title: Implant in a human participant
buildSteps.detail: A small opening is made in the skull, a robot inserts each electrode along a path planned to avoid surface blood vessels, and the electronics package is fixed to the skull and closed beneath the scalp.

buildSteps.title: Record and map
buildSteps.detail: The participant attempts movements or speech while engineers log neural activity, identifying which channels carry which intention.

buildSteps.title: Train and calibrate the decoder
buildSteps.detail: A machine-learning model is fitted so recorded spike patterns map to cursor or limb commands, then retrained as the signals drift over days and weeks.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: The decoder drives a robotic arm, a cursor, or the participant's own muscles through electrical stimulation; where available, stimulation of sensory cortex returns a feeling of touch or limb position.

buildSteps.title: Monitor long term
buildSteps.detail: Signal quality is tracked for months to years, because electrode scarring and implant wear — not the software — are the main failure modes.

prerequisites.why: microelectrode signals can fade over months to years as scar tissue builds around the shanks, so most human use is still in research protocols.
hundreds of channels must stream out and power come in through intact skin without heating tissue beyond safe limits.
models translating spikes into cursor, robotic-arm, handwriting and speech commands have been demonstrated in small human trials, but need frequent recalibration.
stereotactic planning and robotic insertion are established techniques that make consistent electrode placement possible.
robotic arms, exoskeletons and functional electrical stimulators already work; they mainly lack a natural command signal.

prerequisites.tech: Regulatory pathway for implanted neural devices
prerequisites.why: clearance requires years of safety data on infection, explantation and long-term tissue response.

pathway.milestone: small clinical trials, typically a few dozen participants worldwide, restoring cursor control, typing, robotic-arm use and in some cases movement of the person's own hand
pathway.unlocks: proof that chronic human recording can drive useful actions — still research, not a product.

pathway.milestone: fully implanted, wireless systems with higher channel counts and multi-year durability
pathway.unlocks: daily use outside a laboratory and without a technician present.

pathway.milestone: sensory feedback integrated into the control loop
pathway.unlocks: grip force and touch, which is what turns a controlled arm into a usable prosthesis.

pathway.milestone: regulatory clearance for a narrow indication, such as communication for people with severe paralysis
pathway.unlocks: a reimbursed treatment rather than an experiment.

pathway.milestone: general-purpose bidirectional interfaces with stable decades-long electrodes
pathway.unlocks: broader use in paralysis, amputation and other conditions, alongside unresolved questions of long-term safety, cost and neural privacy.
